# Expertise

## Methods

Marchetti's lab trains machine-learned interatomic potentials on ab initio
molecular dynamics data to simulate phase transitions in battery cathode
materials at time and length scales unreachable by direct ab initio
simulation [marchetti2020potential].

## Intellectual lineage

This work extends earlier machine-learned potential frameworks, adapted
specifically to capture the discontinuous energy landscapes that
accompany cathode phase transitions during cycling [marchetti2020potential].

## Recurring critiques

A recurring critique is that many published interatomic potentials are
validated only on equilibrium structures and are not checked against the
non-equilibrium states that actually occur during battery cycling
[marchetti2020potential].

## Career trajectory

Early work applied standard ab initio molecular dynamics to small cathode
unit cells; the shift to machine-learned potentials [marchetti2020potential]
followed once cycling-relevant system sizes made direct simulation
impractical.
